newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says to offer electricity line concession.
newsitem.headline: Peru says to offer electricity line concession.

text.p: Peru's government said Wednesday it is considering asking private companies to compete for a concession for the construction of an electricty line connecting the country's north-central and southern grids.

"We are thinking, on the privatization board, of the line that is going to join Mantaro with Socabaya. It is a very important line that will mean finally connecting the north- central and southern systems and, in this way, ensure an energy supply in the south," Energy and Mines Minister Alberto Pandolfi told reporters, without giving more details about the concession.

In its successful privatization program the government has thus far concentrated on selling assets, but last month it announced plans for a "second wave" of privatizations granting concessions to private companies to carry out public sector infrastuctural projects.

In the program, the government is targeting electricity projects because it expects the country's electricity energy demand to grow by 5.5 percent annually for the next ten years, according to the Energy and Mines Ministry.

In principle, the concessions program would entail the government granting private firms ownership for a given period of an asset that the company constructs or administers, according to Presidency Minister Daniel Hokama.
-- Saul Hudson, Lima newsroom, 511 221-2134 REUTER SH CG
